findings.rule: 1-default-rules.md: "No stubs or placeholders. New code must not ship `TODO`, `FIXME`, "not implemented" or empty bodies standing in for real behaviour."
findings.why: The error path is a placeholder: the catch body is literally `// TODO: handle errors properly later` followed by a hardcoded return, so the new file ships a TODO standing in for real error handling.

findings.rule: 1-default-rules.md: "No swallowed errors. A `catch` (or equivalent) must handle, rethrow or report the error; it must not ignore it or hide it behind a success value."
findings.why: The catch swallows the error entirely: it neither rethrows, logs, nor reports it, and instead returns `{ name: "Unknown" }` as if the fetch succeeded. A network failure, a JSON parse error and a real user named "Unknown" all become indistinguishable, and the caller gets a success value where the request failed.

findings.rule: 1-default-rules.md: "No silent fallbacks on external data. A default value for data from a network, file, user or other system (`??`, `||`, `or`, `getOrElse`) needs a comment saying why the default is correct."
findings.why: `body.user ?? { name: "Unknown" }` supplies a default for JSON parsed from a network response, and neither the line nor the JSDoc explains why `{ name: "Unknown" }` is a correct substitute for a missing `user` field; the response status (`response.ok`) is never checked either, so a 401/404 body also yields this silent default.

findings.rule: 1-default-rules.md: "A behaviour change comes with a test, or says in the diff why it cannot be tested."
findings.why: This diff adds an entirely new exported function with new behaviour (network fetch, error swallowing, fallback object) and the complete diff adds no test file or test case, nor any statement explaining why it cannot be tested.
